title: Quarterly Commitment Ledger & Drift Control for Hosted API Model Catalog
creator: Samira Patel
description: Objective: Create a 'Commitment Ledger' operational artifact and process that ties quarterly Hosted API + Model Catalog commitments to measurables, guardrails, and an explicit drift-control plan. Problem: We keep making time-boxed model/catalog commitments without a clear, auditable way to detect cross-cycle drift (performance regressions, cost slippage, traffic mismatches) and to reconcile commitments against capacity and OKRs. This ticket scopes a single quarterly playbook and the minimum set of dashboard signals and rollout automation to: 1) Record each commitment with owner, SLA/latency target, expected traffic mix, and success metric; 2) Monitor for 'drift' across latency, P95/P99, token cost/unit, and quality regressions tied to canonical eval sets; 3) Emit policy-driven actions (auto-throttle, canary rollback, or schedule remediation) when drift thresholds breach; 4) Define cross-functional cadence for reconciliation (weekly ledger review, post-mortems). Deliverables: Commitment Ledger template (Confluence), a minimal ledger API (schema + Git repo), three dashboard panels in Console (latency, cost-per-token, eval delta), two alert rules (performance drift, cost drift), a canary rollback playbook linked to rollout. Success metrics: ledger adoption by >80% of hosted-model commitments for the quarter; mean-time-to-detect drift < 2 hours for P95 breaches; reduction in token-cost surprises >50% vs. prior quarter. Timeline & milestones: Week 0–2: finalize ledger schema and owner map; Week 3–5: implement dashboard panels and basic alerting; Week 6: run pilot with two model teams; Week 8: retro and broaden to full hosted catalog. Stakeholders: PM (Samira Patel), Eng lead (Diego Morales - onboarding/runtime), Console UX (Ava Nguyen), Applied ML (Priya Desai). Risks & mitigations: Risk — conflicting ownership for metrics across runtime and model teams. Mitigation — explicit owner field in ledger and weekly cross-functional sync. Risk — excessive alert noise. Mitigation — tiered thresholds and initial pilot tuning. Dependencies: runtime metrics instrumentation (ENG-21104), Console panel primitives (ENG-22011), canonical eval ingestion pipeline (ML-9003). Notes: This is intentionally scoped to produce a lightweight, repeatable process that scales between Hosted and Dedicated later. Ledger schema should be exportable to CSV/JSON for audits and exec dashboards.
